en.name: Sunflower oil
en.summary: Sunflower oil keeps 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight. It fails by going rancid rather than by growing anything, and light, heat, air and time are the four things that decide how quickly.
en.pantry: 1 year from purchase, cool, dark and capped. Ordinary sunflower oil is high in polyunsaturated fat, which is exactly what oxygen attacks, so it is less stable than olive or palm oil even though refining removes the compounds that would otherwise go first. High-oleic sunflower oil, sold specifically for frying, is a different composition — mostly monounsaturated — and stands up far better to heat, though it still ages in the bottle. In either case, the cupboard directly above the hob is the worst storage place in the kitchen, and a half-empty bottle ages faster than a full one because the headspace is a supply of oxygen that grows with every pour.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for sunflower oil, and for a bottle in regular use it is unnecessary. Refrigeration slows oxidation, so it is a defensible choice for a very large bottle you are working through slowly, especially through a hot summer; the oil will cloud and thicken in the cold, which is harmless and clears at room temperature. Buying a smaller bottle does more for quality than chilling a big one.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for sunflower oil and freezing is pointless. Oil does not set solid the way water does, so nothing is gained in convenience, and a bottle moved in and out of the freezer collects condensation. Water in an oil bottle is a real problem: it gives spoilage organisms a foothold in a food that otherwise offers them none.
en.thawing: Let a chilled bottle stand at room temperature until it is clear and pours freely. Do not warm oil on the hob or in hot water — heat ages it.
spoilage: A sharp, crayon or paint-like smell — rancid oil, and decisive.
A bitter, scratchy finish at the back of the throat.
A sticky, varnish-like film around the neck and cap.
Colour noticeably darker than when the bottle was opened.
tips: Buy a bottle you will finish within a few months of opening.
Never store oil above the hob.
Use high-oleic sunflower oil if you fry regularly; it takes heat far better.
Keep used frying oil in a separate jar — never pour it back into the fresh bottle.

faq.q: How long does sunflower oil last?
faq.a: 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight.

faq.q: Is sunflower oil good for deep-frying?
faq.a: Ordinary sunflower oil is high in polyunsaturated fat and breaks down relatively quickly under heat. High-oleic sunflower oil is mostly monounsaturated and is much better suited to frying.

faq.q: How can you tell if sunflower oil has gone off?
faq.a: Smell it. A crayon or paint-like note means it is rancid, and it will taste bitter and scratchy. That is a quality failure, not a pathogen risk.

zh.name: 葵花油
zh.summary: 葵花油自購買日起，放陰涼避光、瓶蓋鎖緊，可放 1 年。它的失敗方式是油耗而不是長東西，而決定快慢的是光、熱、空氣和時間這四件事。
zh.pantry: 自購買日起 1 年，陰涼、避光、鎖緊瓶蓋。一般葵花油的多元不飽和脂肪含量高，而那正是氧氣攻擊的對象，所以即使精煉已經去掉了最先劣化的那些成分，它還是不如橄欖油或棕櫚油穩定。專門賣給油炸用的高油酸葵花油則是另一種組成——以單元不飽和為主——耐熱得多，不過在瓶子裡一樣會老化。無論哪一種，爐台正上方的櫃子都是全廚房最糟的存放位置；而且半空的瓶子比滿瓶老得快，因為那段頂空是每倒一次就變大的氧氣來源。
zh.fridge: 葵花油沒有公布的冷藏期限；對一瓶天天在用的油來說也沒有必要。冷藏能拖慢氧化，所以一瓶很大、用得很慢的油放冷藏是說得過去的，尤其是撐過炎熱的夏天；低溫下它會變濁、變稠，那是無害的，回到室溫就清了。不過買小瓶對品質的幫助，仍然大於把大瓶冰起來。
zh.freezer: 葵花油沒有公布的冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有意義。油不像水那樣會凍成硬塊，使用上沒有任何好處；而一瓶進出冷凍的油只會一直結露。油瓶裡有水是真正的問題：它在一個本來什麼都不提供的食物裡，給了腐敗菌立足點。
zh.thawing: 把冰過的瓶子放室溫，等它恢復清澈、倒得順即可。不要拿去爐火上或泡熱水加溫——熱會讓它老化。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆味——油耗了，而且是決定性的。
入口後喉頭有苦味和刮喉感。
瓶頸和瓶蓋周圍出現黏黏、像亮光漆的膜。
顏色比剛開瓶時明顯變深。
tips: 買開封後幾個月內用得完的容量。
絕對不要把油放在爐台上方。
常油炸的話請用高油酸葵花油，它耐熱得多。
用過的炸油另外裝罐——絕對不要倒回新油瓶。

faq.a: 自購買日起，陰涼避光、瓶蓋鎖緊，1 年。
一般葵花油多元不飽和脂肪高，受熱分解得比較快。高油酸葵花油以單元不飽和為主，比較適合油炸。
聞一下。像蠟筆或油漆的味道就是油耗，吃起來會苦、會刮喉嚨。那是品質問題，不是病原菌風險。
